title: Newmark Arranges $85 Million Refinancing of 300 Lafayette Street in SoHo, Manhattan
summary: Newmark announces the Company has arranged an $85 million loan on behalf of InterVest Capital Partners to refinance 300 Lafayette Street, a boutique…
body_markdown:
**September 24, 2026 9:00 AM**
Newmark announces the Company has arranged an $85 million loan on behalf of InterVest Capital Partners to refinance 300 Lafayette Street, a boutique mixed-use office and retail property in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. Hudson Bay Capital provided the financing.


Newmark Co-Head of[Global Debt & Structured Finance](https://www.nmrk.com/services/investor-solutions/capital-markets/debt-and-structured-finance)[Jordan Roeschlaub](https://www.nmrk.com/people/jordan-roeschlaub) , Vice Chairman[Nick Scribani](https://www.nmrk.com/people/nick-scribani) , Managing Director[John Caraviello](https://www.nmrk.com/people/john-caraviello) and Associate Director[Ryan Bub](https://www.nmrk.com/people/ryan-bub) arranged the financing on behalf of the borrower.


“300 Lafayette Street is as good as boutique product gets in Lower Manhattan, new construction by COOKFOX with a fully occupied office component anchored by Microsoft and retail on one of the most heavily trafficked corners in SoHo,” said Scribani. “Lender interest was deep and competitive, and Zach Cion and the Hudson Bay Capital team delivered speed and certainty of execution for the sponsor.”


Delivered in 2019 and designed by COOKFOX Architects, 300 Lafayette Street is a seven-story, 82,000-square-foot property featuring floor-to-ceiling glass, virtually column-free floorplates and more than 10,000 square feet of landscaped outdoor terraces. Microsoft occupies the entire 63,000-square-foot office component across floors two through seven, with Neko Health, New Era and Goldwin comprising the retail tenancy.


“300 Lafayette is an irreplaceable asset, anchored by an AAA investment-grade credit tenant, and a new-construction building on a corner that defines the entrance to SoHo. Buildings like this are nearly impossible to replicate at today’s replacement costs.” said Rob Rothschild, Managing Director and Head of Real Estate at InterVest Capital Partners. “This financing reflects the strength of the property and its tenancy. Hudson Bay Capital was a strong partner throughout, and the Newmark team ran an efficient process from start to finish.”


Situated at the intersection of Lafayette, East Houston and Crosby Streets, the property serves as a gateway to SoHo, NoHo and NoLita, with immediate access to the Broadway-Lafayette Street and Bleecker Street subway stations.


**About InterVest Capital Partners** InterVest capital partners (“InterVest”) is a New York-based global alternative investment manager specializing in real estate, specialty finance, and asset-based finance. Since its inception, InterVest has invested $27.5 billion in alternative strategies and is 100% employee-owned and controlled, with teams in New York, London, and Luxembourg investing across North America, the United Kingdom, and Europe. To date, the company has invested over $12.8 billion in US real estate mandates.


**About Newmark** Newmark Group, Inc.
